test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 10th December 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A sum of ₹2,50,000 is invested for one and a half years at 12% per annum compound interest. What is the difference between the amounts received when the interest is compounded semi-annually and when it is compounded annually?
solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Effective CI rate (annually) for 1.5 years at 12% = 12% + 6% + (12 × 6) ÷ 100 = 18.72% Effective CI rate (semi-annually) for 3 half-years at 6% = 3(6) + 3(6)² ÷ 100 + (6)³ ÷ 10000 = 18 + 1.08 + 0.0216 = 19.1016% Difference in effective rate = 19.1016% − 18.72% = 0.3816% Difference in amount = 0.3816% of 2,50,000 = (0.3816 ÷ 100) × 250000 = ₹954 **∴ The correct answer is ₹954.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** **Given:** Principal (P) = ₹2,50,000 Rate (R) = 12% per annum Time (T) = 1.5 years Compounded Annually (1.5 years): ₹2,50,000 • +12% (1st yr) ₹2,80,000 • +6% (½ yr) ₹2,96,800 Compounded Semi-Annually (3 half-years): ₹2,50,000 • +6% ₹2,65,000 • +6% ₹2,80,900 • +6% ₹2,97,754 Difference = ₹2,97,754 − ₹2,96,800 = ₹954 **Calculations:** ⇒ Amount compounded annually (A₁) = P × (1 + R/100)¹ × (1 + (R/2)/100) ⇒ A₁ = 250000 × (1 + 12/100) × (1 + 6/100) ⇒ A₁ = 250000 × 1.12 × 1.06 = 250000 × 1.1872 ⇒ A₁ = ₹2,96,800 ⇒ Amount compounded semi-annually (A₂) = P × (1 + (R/2)/100)²T ⇒ A₂ = 250000 × (1 + 6/100)³ ⇒ A₂ = 250000 × (1.06)³ = 250000 × 1.191016 ⇒ A₂ = ₹2,97,754 ⇒ Difference in amounts = A₂ − A₁ ⇒ Difference = 297754 − 296800 = ₹954 **∴ The correct answer is ₹954.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** Effective Rate Method For 3 equal periods at rate R%, the effective compound interest rate is calculated as: 3R + 3R²/100 + R³/10000. Half-Yearly Compounding When interest is compounded semi-annually, the annual rate of interest is divided by 2 (R/2) and the number of years is multiplied by 2 (2T). Fractional Year Compounding If time is given in fractions like 1.5 years, the formula used for annual compounding is: A = P(1 + R/100)¹ × (1 + (R/2)/100)¹. 152:T166c,
